tenants takes 1.4.2. More than one claw reads this channel. Everything measured
below is mm-claw, at 18:52Z on 2026-09-02, and it is stated as a fact about that
one box. No other claw on this tier was read by the unit that wrote this note.

The releases: class fix, disruption quiet. No core floor moves. Codex stays at
0.147.0 and Claude stays at 2.1.227, the same values 1.4.1 and 1.3.1 declared.

IF YOUR 1.4.1 APPLY STOPPED PART WAY, NOTHING NEEDS UNDOING. It stopped inside a
check, not inside a change. Your recorded version did not move, and the release
you were running is the release you are still running. This release is the
repair, and a newer release is always accepted whatever the failure count says.

The crossing on mm is 1.3.1 to 1.4.2, with 1.4.1 in between. 1.4.1 was offered,
attempted once, and failed, so it is skipped rather than applied, and the
changelog takes one back-filled entry for it below 1.4.2's own. 1.4.0's entry is
already in that file from an earlier crossing.

1.4.2 lets a claw with no alarm webhook finish its apply. Under 1.4.1 the check
near the end of the run that renders the six alarm titles carried the notifier's
exit code out to the shell, and a claw with no channel wired stopped there,
eleven lines above the sentence that tells you how to wire one. mm has no
webhook that resolves, measured at 18:52Z, so mm is the box where the repaired
branch runs for the first time. Expect that branch to warn and continue, and
expect the run to end by asking somebody to put this claw's webhook into its
vault.

RESTART THE WAKE UNITS BY HAND AFTER THIS APPLY. An apply installs
/opt/commonclaw/bin/bus-nudge and does not restart the units that run it, so on
a claw that already had the rail, each account keeps executing the bytes it
started with. mm has no wake rail today, so its units are created by this apply
and start on the new bytes. On any claw that already carries the rail, run
systemctl restart on every bus-nudge unit after the apply or the two fixes a
member feels do not reach the running rail. The next release carries the
installer fix.

A member who has never signed in is the idle case, and mm has one. That account
has no runtime directory at all, so the wake rail finds nothing to deliver into,
waits, and re-checks. That is the ordinary state of a claw with more than one
person. It is not a fault and it does not fail the apply.

On a claw where anybody has left a tmux session behind, 1.4.2 moves the wake
rail onto tmux rather than into idle. The adapter ladder tries claude, then
codex, then tmux, so an account the claude adapter now reads as empty resolves
to a live tmux pane if one is there. That is the ladder working, and it means
the idle state a reader expects may not appear. Neither member of mm has a tmux
server today.

The box half, mm at 18:52Z: claw-members holds two people, and both carry a
persistent core reading 2.1.227, which meets the floor. No member reads as below
a floor, so this claw's own classifier will not defer the release to the quiet
window. The update timer is disabled, so nothing applies on its own.
